title: Four of five selected unlabelled CHIME pairs differ by more than three combined formal DM errors
abstract: We test a constant dispersion measure (DM) screen for five close unlabelled pairs in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. Four pairs differ by more than three combined formal DM errors. The same screen retains 313 of 632 close pairs with known common-source labels. Equal source weights give 45.1 percent mean retention across 38 sources. An added DM error of 0.5 pc cm^-3 per event retains all five unlabelled pairs and gives 94.1 percent mean retention for known sources. This added error is a sensitivity parameter, not a measured instrument or plasma term. The result shows limited value of a formal-error-only constant-DM screen for source association in this selected catalog. It does not confirm a new source, lens or physical DM change. Full location maps and independent instrument observations were not fitted. Code, aggregate evidence, simulated counts, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Pair retention changes with an added DM error. The shaded band is a conditional shuffle reference range. Known-source retention gives each source equal weight.
